headline: US stocks ended mixed as oil jumped on renewed US‑Iran tensions and Fed minutes kept rate hike risk in focus
raw_text:
- Major US indices finished mixed, with the Dow (DIA) and S&P 500 (SPY) lower and the Nasdaq (QQQ) slightly higher as risk assets contended with an oil spike and geopolitical tensions.
- WTI crude (@CL) climbed over 3–4% after President Trump declared the Iran ceasefire "over" and the US and Iran exchanged strikes, including additional US action after the close.
- Energy led the market, with Chevron (CVX) gaining about 1% while ExxonMobil (XOM) traded near flat amid higher crude prices.
- Broadcom (AVGO) rose around 5% after announcing an expanded partnership with Apple (AAPL), supporting large-cap technology shares.
- Nvidia (NVDA) gained about 3.6% on reports of increased Chinese chip purchases, while Micron (MU) rose modestly and AMD (AMD) was little changed.
- Financials and cyclicals weakened, including a roughly 2.5% drop in JPMorgan (JPM), and defensive sectors such as health care, utilities, and consumer staples also closed lower.
- Fed minutes showed some officials remain open to another rate hike amid persistent inflation concerns, contributing to a cautious market tone.
- After-hours, Levi Strauss (LEVI) fell about 5.5% despite beating earnings estimates and raising guidance.
- AZZ Inc. (AZZ) traded higher after-hours following a strong earnings beat.
- Traders looked ahead to Thursday’s PepsiCo (PEP) results and further developments in US‑Iran tensions and Fed policy expectations for direction.
